title: Separating transferable missing physics from object-, backend-, contact-, actuation-, and sensor-specific discrepancy
scientific_question: Can a Bayesian physical twin diagnose which mechanism generated a residual and transfer only the component representing persistent missing physics across physical objects and simulator backends?

primary_hypotheses.H1_shared_physics: A nonzero residual component is stable across source objects and remains beneficial without coefficient refitting on independently held-out DLOs.
primary_hypotheses.H2_backend_specificity: A simulator-specific component improves predictions only under the backend on which it was identified and is rejected after a backend change.
primary_hypotheses.H3_object_specificity: An object-specific component improves within-object held-out trajectories but does not transfer to a new object.
primary_hypotheses.H4_mechanism_diagnosis: The source-only posterior diagnosis predicts which discrepancy components will transfer; forcing an incompatible diagnosis removes or reverses the gain.
primary_hypotheses.H5_exact_fallback: When no transferable component passes the source-only evidence and support gates, the emitted target prediction is byte-identical to the registered physical fallback.

additive_discrepancy_model.equation: delta = delta_shared_physics + delta_object + delta_backend + delta_contact + delta_actuation + delta_sensor + epsilon

groups.name: shared_physics
groups.meaning: persistent missing dynamics represented in normalized mechanical coordinates

groups.name: object
groups.meaning: DLO-specific material, geometry, or mounting remainder not represented by the physical backbone

groups.name: contact
groups.meaning: unmodeled contact-regime effect conditional on an explicit contact-support signature

groups.name: actuation
groups.meaning: command-to-motion discrepancy conditional on an explicit actuation-calibration identity

groups.name: sensor
groups.meaning: measurement-space bias or noise correlation that must not alter physical rollout state

inference.family: group automatic relevance determination Bayesian linear residual operator
diagnosis_outputs: group posterior effective degrees of freedom

data_custody.protected_target_rule: No DLO4/DLO5 target score, target residual, or target-dependent hyperparameter may be opened until the parent run is terminal and its joint pre-score seal verifies.
data_custody.backend_holdout: A separately sealed alternate-backend rollout generated from the same released initial conditions and commands; backend identity is fixed before scoring.
data_custody.independent_unit: complete trajectory within each physical DLO, with DLO-stratified reporting
forbidden: pooling DLO4 and DLO5 to conceal a failure
treating frames or nodes as independent samples
transferring sensor discrepancy into physical state
relabeling a failed diagnosis after target opening

target_phase.authorization: Requires source gate pass, terminal protected parent run, verified parent joint seal, and a separately committed target request file.
target_phase.primary_transfer: Freeze shared_physics coefficients learned without DLO4/DLO5 and apply them without coefficient refitting.

claim_ladder.source_only: The decomposition is identifiable enough on already-open DLO2/DLO3 to distinguish transferable from nontransferable residual mechanisms.
claim_ladder.object_transfer: A frozen shared missing-physics component improves DLO4 and DLO5 without residual coefficient refitting.
claim_ladder.backend_transfer: The same shared component survives a simulator-backend change while the diagnosed backend-specific component does not.
claim_ladder.full_claim: The twin separates reusable missing physics from object- and simulator-specific discrepancy and uses that diagnosis to decide what may safely transfer.

failure_policy: Every negative, mixed, or abstaining result is retained. A failed source gate forbids target opening. A failed target object or backend remains separate and cannot be repaired within this protocol version.
